title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask favours politely, ask permission, offer and accept or refuse hospitality, and invite people over — with the right level of respect.
intro:
Marathi politeness lives in the verb. 'Help me' can be मदत कर (to a friend), मदत करा (polite), or the gentle question **मदत कराल का?** ('will you help?'), which is how you'd ask a stranger a favour.

This unit also covers Marathi hospitality, which runs on **आग्रह** — the host's warm insistence that you eat more, stay longer and come again. Knowing how to refuse gracefully (नको, राहू दे) is as important as knowing how to accept.

grammar.title: Polite requests: 'Would you…?'
grammar.body:
From blunt to very polite:

**Informal imperative:** दार उघड. 'Open the door.'
**Polite imperative:** दार उघडा. — add ना / जरा to soften: जरा दार उघडा ना.
**Future + का?** ('will you…?'): दार उघडाल का? (polite) / उघडशील का? (informal). This is the standard way to ask a favour.
**'It would be good if…':** the past form of the verb + **तर बरं होईल**: तुम्ही आलात तर बरं होईल 'it would be nice if you came'.
**Formal / written:** **कृपया** + stem + **आवे**: कृपया शांतता राखावी 'please maintain silence', कृपया पादत्राणे बाहेर काढावीत 'please remove footwear'.

Respectful address: add **-जी**, **-साहेब**, **-राव** (to men) or **-ताई**, **-बाई** (to women) to names, and use **अहो** to get attention.

examples.en: Could I have some water, please?
Could you drop me at the station?
Will you do something for me? (informal)

examples.native: तुम्ही थोडं हळू बोललात तर बरं होईल.
examples.roman: tumhī thoḍaṃ haḷū bollāt tar baraṃ hoīl.
examples.en: It would help if you spoke a little slowly.

grammar.title: Permission, offers and refusing
grammar.body:
**May I / shall I?** stem + **ऊ** + **का?**: मी आत येऊ का? 'may I come in?', मी बसू का? 'may I sit?', दार बंद करू का? 'shall I close the door?'

**Let me / let him:** stem + **ऊ** + **दे / द्या**: मला बोलू द्या 'let me speak', त्याला जाऊ दे 'let him go'.

**Offering:** use -णार का? or the future: चहा घेणार का? / चहा घ्याल का? Or simply the polite imperative: बसा ना, चहा घ्या.

**Refusing politely:** नको, राहू दे · आत्ता नको, धन्यवाद · पुढच्या वेळी नक्की 'next time for sure'. A first refusal is often expected to be overridden by the host's आग्रह!

examples.en: May I park the car here?
Would you like a little more?
Not now — next time for sure.

dialogue.title: Invited for Ganpati
dialogue.setting: Mrs Joshi invites her neighbour David to her home during the Ganesh festival; the next evening, at dinner.

lines.speaker: Mrs Joshi
lines.native: नमस्कार! उद्या आमच्याकडे गणपती येणार आहेत.
lines.roman: namaskār! udyā āmchyākaḍe gaṇpatī yeṇār āhet.
lines.en: Hello! Tomorrow Ganpati is coming to our home.

lines.speaker: Mrs Joshi
lines.native: तुम्ही संध्याकाळी आरतीला आणि जेवायला याल का?
lines.roman: tumhī sandhyākāḷī āratīlā āṇi jevāylā yāl kā?
lines.en: Would you come in the evening for the aarti and dinner?

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: हो, जरूर! मी काही आणू का?
lines.roman: ho, dzarūr! mī kāhī āṇū kā?
lines.en: Yes, certainly! Shall I bring anything?

lines.speaker: Mrs Joshi
lines.native: नाही नाही, काही आणू नका. फक्त सात वाजता या.
lines.roman: nāhī nāhī, kāhī āṇū nakā. phakta sāt vādztā yā.
lines.en: No, no, don't bring anything. Just come at seven.

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: मी माझ्या मित्राला पण आणलं तर चालेल का?
lines.roman: mī mājhyā mitrālā paṇ āṇlaṃ tar tsālel kā?
lines.en: Would it be all right if I brought my friend too?

lines.speaker: Mrs Joshi
lines.en: With pleasure! Both of you come.

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: नको, खरंच पोट भरलं. पण मोदक खूप छान झाले होते!
lines.roman: nako, kharaṃts poṭ bharlaṃ. paṇ modak khūp chhān dzhāle hote!
lines.en: No, really, I'm full. But the modaks were delicious!

lines.speaker: Mrs Joshi
lines.native: अहो, एक तरी घ्या, आग्रह आहे!
lines.roman: aho, ek tarī ghyā, āgraha āhe!
lines.en: Oh, at least have one, I insist!

culture: During **गणेशोत्सव**, many families install a Ganesh idol at home for 1½, 5, 7 or 10 days, and inviting friends and neighbours for the evening **आरती** (devotional song with lamps) and prasad is a central part of the festival. The sweet dumpling **मोदक** is Ganpati's favourite. When visiting, it's polite to take sweets or fruit even if told not to bring anything, and to accept at least some food — refusing everything can seem cold. Remove shoes before entering, and touch an elder's feet (नमस्कार करणे) if the family does so.
